title: Habitats and Communities
seo_title: Grade 4 Science: Habitats and Communities Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Describe habitats as places that give plants and animals food, water, shelter and space; identify living and non-living parts of a habitat; describe populations and communities in local Ontario habitats. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand B: Life Systems – Habitats and Communities)
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 science worksheets on habitats, living and non-living things, populations and communities in Ontario forests, wetlands and lakes. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A habitat meets a living thing's needs.
key_sub: Food, water, shelter and space; many populations together make a community.
body_html:
How to think about it

A habitat is the place where a plant or animal lives and finds what it needs.

  • Animals need food, water, shelter and space. Plants need sunlight, water, air, nutrients and space.
  • A habitat has living parts (plants, animals, fungi) and non-living parts (water, rocks, soil, air, sunlight).
  • A population is all of one kind of living thing in an area. A community is all the populations living together.
  • Ontario habitats include the boreal forest, mixed forests, wetlands, lakes, rivers and meadows.
Example

A beaver lives in a pond. Name its needs that the pond meets.

food: tree bark and pond plants

water: the pond

shelter: its lodge

Answer: food, water, shelter and space

Example

All the frogs in a marsh are a …

one kind of animal in one place

Answer: population

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up population (one kind) and community (all kinds).
  • Thinking water, rocks and sunlight are living because they help living things.
  • Thinking any animal can live in any habitat.

faq.q: What is the difference between a habitat and a community?
faq.a: A habitat is the place. A community is all the living things that live in that place together.

faq.q: What are the needs of animals?
faq.a: Animals need food, water, shelter and space. Plants also need sunlight and air.

faq.q: What habitats are found in Ontario?
faq.a: Ontario has boreal forest in the north, mixed and deciduous forests in the south, and many lakes, rivers and wetlands.

items.q: Which of these lives in the ocean: a newt, a whale, an Arctic fox or seaweed?
items.e: Each habitat has its own plants and animals.

items.q: What is a community?
c: the soil and rocks in a place
all the plants and animals that live together in one habitat
only the plants in a forest
items.e: A community includes all the living things in a habitat.

items.q: How do the features of an owl help it in its habitat? It has big eyes and silent wings.
c: They help it breathe and swim under water.
They help it keep warm in the cold Arctic.
They help it hunt in the dark woods at night.
They help it stay safe when waves bash it on the rocks.
items.e: Animals are suited to their habitats.

items.q: Which habitat does a penguin live in?
items.e: Living things live where they can get what they need.

items.q: Which habitat does a whale live in?
items.e: Living things live where they can get what they need.

items.q: Which living thing has features that help it breathe and swim under water?
items.e: A fish has gills and fins.

items.q: Which habitat does a crab live in?
items.e: Living things live where they can get what they need.

items.q: Which habitat is very cold and icy?
items.e: Near the North Pole.

items.q: Which is a non-living part of a forest habitat?
items.e: Rocks, water, air and sunlight are non-living.

items.q: Do polar bears and penguins live together?
c: No. Polar bears live in the Arctic; penguins live in the Antarctic.
items.e: Opposite ends of the Earth.

items.q: Which habitat does an oak tree live in?
items.e: Living things live where they can get what they need.

items.q: A loon needs clean lakes with fish. What would happen if the lake became polluted?
c: The loon might not find enough food and might leave or die.
The loon would start eating plants.
items.e: Habitats must meet an animal's needs.

items.q: Which habitat is very hot and dry?
items.e: Little rain.

items.q: A beaver builds a lodge in a pond. What need does the lodge meet?
items.e: The lodge keeps the beaver safe and warm.

items.q: Which of these lives in a pond: a dolphin, a frog, a shark or a squirrel?
items.e: Each habitat has its own plants and animals.

items.q: How do the features of a crab help it in its habitat? It has a hard shell.
c: They help it stay safe when waves bash it on the rocks.
They help it climb trees and balance on branches.
They help it keep warm in the cold Arctic.
They help it live where it hardly rains.
items.e: Animals are suited to their habitats.

items.q: Which living thing has features that help it climb trees and balance on branches?
items.e: A squirrel has sharp claws and a long tail.

items.q: A chickadee stays in Ontario all winter. Which part of its habitat helps it survive the cold?
c: evergreen trees for shelter and seeds to eat
items.e: Trees give shelter and food.

items.q: Which Ontario habitat is wet land covered with shallow water and cattails?
items.e: Marshes have shallow water and tall plants.

items.q: What is a population?
c: all the members of one kind of living thing in an area
all the different animals in a forest
items.e: For example, all the white-tailed deer in a park.

items.q: Which word best describes all the frogs living in the pond?
items.e: A population is one kind of organism in a habitat at the same time.

items.q: What is it usually like under a log?
items.e: Microhabitats each have their own conditions.

items.q: What is a habitat?
c: the place where a plant or animal lives and gets what it needs
items.e: A habitat gives food, water, shelter and space.

items.q: Where are you most likely to find a centipede?
c: under a log or a stone
on the leaves of a plant
in a web in a hedge
items.e: Small creatures live in the microhabitat that gives them what they need.

items.q: Which word best describes all the different plants and animals living in the forest at Bukit Timah?
items.e: A community is all the populations living together in a habitat.

items.q: Which word best describes all the millipedes living in the forest at Bukit Timah?
items.e: A population is one kind of organism in a habitat at the same time.

items.q: All the Canada geese in one wetland are a …
items.e: One kind of animal in one place is a population.

items.q: Which word best describes one butterfly in the school field?
items.e: One living thing is an organism, not a population.

items.q: What is it usually like in leaf litter?
items.e: Microhabitats each have their own conditions.

items.q: Would you find many sow bugs on a sunny path?
c: Sow bugs live only in ponds.
Yes, they like dark, damp places.
Sow bugs live only in trees.
No, sow bugs dry out in bright, warm places.
items.e: Sow bugs need damp places to stop them drying out.

items.q: Which word best describes all the dragonflies living in the pond?
items.e: A population is one kind of organism in a habitat at the same time.

items.q: Would you find many sow bugs in leaf litter?
c: Yes, they like dark, damp places.
Sow bugs live only in ponds.
No, sow bugs dry out in bright, warm places.
Sow bugs live only in trees.
items.e: Sow bugs need damp places to stop them drying out.

items.q: Where are you most likely to find an earthworm?
c: in a nest under a patio stone
on the leaves of a plant
items.e: Small creatures live in the microhabitat that gives them what they need.

items.q: Which word best describes one guppy in the pond?
items.e: One living thing is an organism, not a population.

items.q: Which word means 'a living thing'?
items.e: Plants, animals and fungi are organisms.

items.q: Where are you most likely to find a ladybug?
c: in a nest under a patio stone
under a log or a stone
on the leaves of a plant
items.e: Small creatures live in the microhabitat that gives them what they need.

items.q: Which pair are both non-living parts of a habitat?
items.e: Living things grow and reproduce; water and sunlight do not.

items.q: Which word best describes all the barnacles living on the rocky shore?
items.e: A population is one kind of organism in a habitat at the same time.

items.q: Which is a living part of a pond?
items.e: Algae are living things.

items.q: Which is a habitat for frogs in Ontario?
c: a pond with plants around the edge
the top of a mountain in winter
items.e: Frogs need water and damp places.

items.q: What is a population?
c: all the plants and animals in a habitat
all the animals in a habitat
a group of one kind of organism living in a habitat at the same time
items.e: All the guppies in a pond form a population.

items.q: Which of these is a population on the rocky shore?
c: all the seaweed plants and barnacles on the rocky shore
the rocks and sea water of the shore
one seaweed plant on the rocky shore
all the seaweed plants on the rocky shore
items.e: A population is made up of one kind of organism only.

items.q: Which statement about a habitat is correct?
c: A habitat has only one kind of organism.
A habitat provides food, water, shelter and air for organisms.
A habitat is always very large.
Organisms do not need a habitat.
items.e: Habitats can be big (a forest) or small (a rotting log).

items.q: Which of these is a population in the school field?
c: the water and soil of the school field
one love grass plant in the school field
all the love grass plants and earthworms in the school field
all the love grass plants in the school field
items.e: A population is made up of one kind of organism only.

items.q: Which environmental factors affect where organisms live?
c: only the size of the animals
only the colour of the soil
items.e: These are called physical factors.

items.q: What is a community?
c: only the animals in a habitat
all the populations of plants and animals living together in a habitat
one kind of organism in a habitat
items.e: Plants are part of a community too.

items.q: Why do the barnacles on a rocky shore close up at low tide?
c: to keep in water so they do not dry out
items.e: At low tide they are out of the water.

only the animals in the rotting log

items.q: Earthworms come up to the surface of a field after heavy rain. Which factor has changed?
c: amount of water in the soil
items.e: The soil is full of water, so they come up.

items.q: Why can a fish not live in a forest?
c: A fish needs water to breathe and move.
items.e: Each living thing is suited to its habitat.

items.q: Which of these is a population in the rotting log?
c: all the millipedes and earthworms in the rotting log
the water and soil of the rotting log
all the millipedes in the rotting log
one millipede in the rotting log

items.q: Which of these is not part of a community?
c: the water lilies in a pond
items.e: Water is non-living; a community is only living things.

items.q: Which of these is a community in the school field?
c: only the animals in the school field
all the love grass plants in the school field
the school field and the air above it
all the plants and animals living in the school field
items.e: A community has all the populations: plants and animals together.

items.q: Which of these is a community on the rocky shore?
c: all the plants and animals living on the rocky shore
all the crabs on the rocky shore
only the animals on the rocky shore
the rocky shore and the air above it
items.e: A community has all the populations: plants and animals together.

items.q: Which animal lives in the boreal forest of northern Ontario?
items.e: Moose live in forests with lakes and wetlands.

items.q: Can every animal live in every habitat?
c: No. Some survive well, some less well and some not at all.
items.e: Traits fit living things to certain habitats.

items.q: Benjamin visits the rain forest. Which living thing could NOT survive well there?
items.e: Its traits fit a different habitat.

items.q: In which habitat would a camel survive best?
items.e: A camel lives in the desert, where it can get what it needs.

items.q: In which habitat would a jellyfish survive best?
items.e: A jellyfish lives in the ocean, where it can get what it needs.

items.q: What is a habitat?
c: the place where a living thing gets the food, water, shelter and space it needs
only the food an animal eats
items.e: Deserts, oceans and forests are habitats.

items.q: Why can a shark survive well in the ocean?
c: It has a long beak to reach fruit in tall trees.
It stores fat in its hump and can go a long time without water.
It can run fast on hot sand.
items.e: This trait fits the ocean habitat.

items.q: What might happen if a pond dries up?
c: Fish will grow legs at once.
Fish and frogs may die or have to move.
items.e: When a habitat changes, some living things cannot survive.

items.q: Why can a roadrunner survive well in the desert?
c: It hangs from branches with long claws.
It can run fast on hot sand.
It grows well in shady, damp places.
It eats grass and grows a thick winter coat.
items.e: This trait fits the desert habitat.

items.q: In which habitat would a tadpole survive best?
items.e: A tadpole lives in the pond, where it can get what it needs.

items.q: In which habitat would an owl survive best?
items.e: An owl lives in the forest, where it can get what it needs.

items.q: In which habitat would a lion survive best?
items.e: A lion lives in the grassland, where it can get what it needs.

items.q: In which habitat would a sea turtle survive best?
items.e: A sea turtle lives in the ocean, where it can get what it needs.

items.q: Why can a walrus survive well in the Arctic?
c: It has thick blubber for icy water.
It grows well in shady, damp places.
It hangs from branches with long claws.
items.e: This trait fits the Arctic habitat.

items.q: Why can a cactus survive well in the desert?
c: It stores water in its thick stem.
It hangs from branches with long claws.
It has thick fur and a layer of fat.
items.e: This trait fits the desert habitat.

items.q: Jayden visits the grassland. Which living thing could NOT survive well there?
items.e: Its traits fit a different habitat.

items.q: Maya visits the rain forest. Which living thing could NOT survive well there?
items.e: Its traits fit a different habitat.

items.q: Why can't a fish live on land?
c: It needs water to breathe with its gills.
It can live on land for a few weeks.
items.e: Gills only work in water.

items.q: Why can a bison survive well in the grassland?
c: It can run fast on hot sand.
It eats grass and grows a thick winter coat.
It has leaves that float on water.
It hangs from branches with long claws.
items.e: This trait fits the grassland habitat.

items.q: Why can an arctic fox survive well in the Arctic?
c: It can run fast on hot sand.
It eats grass and runs fast in open land.
It has thick blubber for icy water.
items.e: This trait fits the Arctic habitat.

items.q: Noah visits the grassland. Which living thing could NOT survive well there?
items.e: Its traits fit a different habitat.

items.q: A gardener cleared all the dead leaves from under a tree. What would most likely happen to the millipedes living there?
c: Their population decreases because they lose food and shelter.
items.e: Millipedes feed on and shelter in dead leaves.

items.q: Emma counted 40 guppies in a pond in January and 12 in June. The pond became very shallow in June. What is the best explanation?
c: There was less water and less space, so fewer guppies survived.

items.e: A change in a habitat affects the population.

c: Under the log it is dark, damp and has food.
The path is damp and dark.
items.e: Conditions matter.

items.q: How could you make a fair test of whether sow bugs prefer dark or light?
c: Count only once without a tray.
Put the same sow bugs in a tray with one dark side and one light side, and count after the same time.
Use different trays at different times.
items.e: Fair test.

items.q: Is a sow bug an insect?
c: No. It has 14 legs, so it is not an insect.
